headline: Victims demand justice: 11 parties submit memorandum to Parliament on disappearances
summary: Enforced disappearance victims and their families marched to the National Parliament to demand the trial of those involved in disappearances and killings.
details: Victims of enforced disappearances and their families, along with leaders from an 11-party alliance, marched from Banglamotor to the National Parliament building on August 30.
The march was organized by the National Committee for the Prevention of International Enforced Disappearances to mark the International Day of the Prevention of Enforced Disappearances.
Protesters demanded that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and all those involved in disappearances and killings be brought to justice to ensure such crimes never happen again.
They called for the immediate reinstatement of ordinances issued by the interim government regarding the prevention and remedy of enforced disappearances.
Speakers at the event criticized current laws and urged the government to stop hiding facts and instead provide exemplary punishment to the agencies, political parties, and individuals responsible.
A delegation of members of parliament was later approached, and the 11-party alliance submitted a memorandum to the Speaker of the Parliament through them.
caption:
No more fascism, no more disappearances. Victims and 11 political parties march to Parliament demanding justice.

Victims of enforced disappearances and their families, along with leaders from an 11-party alliance, marched from Banglamotor to the National Parliament building on August 30.

The march was organized by the National Committee for the Prevention of International Enforced Disappearances to mark the International Day of the Prevention of Enforced Disappearances.

Protesters demanded that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and all those involved in disappearances and killings be brought to justice to ensure such crimes never happen again.

They called for the immediate reinstatement of ordinances issued by the interim government regarding the prevention and remedy of enforced disappearances.

Speakers at the event criticized current laws and urged the government to stop hiding facts and instead provide exemplary punishment to the agencies, political parties, and individuals responsible.

A delegation of members of parliament was later approached, and the 11-party alliance submitted a memorandum to the Speaker of the Parliament through them.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline_marked: New lead in Sagar-Runi case: [[Cultural personality linked to murders]] after 14 years
headline: New lead in Sagar-Runi case: Cultural personality linked to murders after 14 years
summary: The ICT chief prosecutor reveals preliminary evidence suggesting a prominent cultural figure's involvement in the 2012 killing of the journalist couple.
details: Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), Md Aminul Islam, stated that investigators have found preliminary evidence linking a cultural personality to the murder of Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.
While the prosecutor confirmed the lead, he declined to reveal the individual's identity to protect the integrity of the ongoing investigation.
The breakthrough reportedly emerged while investigators were probing a separate case, providing a new clue in a mystery that has remained unsolved for over a decade.
Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were killed at their flat in Dhaka's Poshchim Rajabazar on February 11, 2012.
Despite the new claim from the prosecution, some investigation officials from the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) have stated they have not yet received such information.
The PBI officials mentioned they would coordinate with the prosecution team to clarify the findings as the investigation continues.
caption:
A 14-year-old mystery may finally be unraveling. Evidence now points to a 'cultural personality' in the Sagar-Runi murder case.

Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), Md Aminul Islam, stated that investigators have found preliminary evidence linking a cultural personality to the murder of Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.

While the prosecutor confirmed the lead, he declined to reveal the individual's identity to protect the integrity of the ongoing investigation.

The breakthrough reportedly emerged while investigators were probing a separate case, providing a new clue in a mystery that has remained unsolved for over a decade.

Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were killed at their flat in Dhaka's Poshchim Rajabazar on February 11, 2012.

Despite the new claim from the prosecution, some investigation officials from the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) have stated they have not yet received such information.

The PBI officials mentioned they would coordinate with the prosecution team to clarify the findings as the investigation continues.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
